paper.title_en: Polarization waves in open-barrier quantum-dot cellular automata
paper.abstract_en: Quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) are almost always operated as bistable digital logic. We develop a closed-form theory of small-signal polarization waves in the open-barrier regime, where tunnelling within each cell is comparable to or stronger than the electrostatic kink coupling between cells, so that a line of cells responds linearly instead of latching. Linearizing the coherence-vector equations of the intercellular Hartree approximation (ICHA) about the unpolarized state gives a lattice dispersion with a low-frequency cutoff, an evanescent band below it and a Klein-Gordon long-wavelength limit, and relaxation toward the instantaneous equilibrium damps the waves at a rate that depends on the wavenumber. The exact Jordan-Wigner solution and exact diagonalization confirm the mode as a sharp quasiparticle, with ICHA frequencies within 6% of the exact ones once the tunnelling energy is at least twice the kink energy, and show that the exact chain also carries waves over a range of couplings where the ICHA predicts latching. A leading low-temperature estimate of thermal dephasing sets a ceiling on the operating temperature of about 13.6 K per terahertz of gap for a carrier that keeps its phase over 30 periods. At junctions the waves scatter through a lattice scattering matrix that reaches the familiar transmission-line value only at mid-band.
